title: Forensic MLX Server Lifecycle Hardening: Process Group Teardown, Port Listen Scoping, and Scheduled Idle Reaping
target_platform: macOS / Apple Silicon MLX Process & Memory Management
hypothesis: Refactoring mlx_server_manager.py to: (1) scope port discovery via `lsof -ti -sTCP:LISTEN :<port>`, (2) terminate the complete process group (`os.killpg`) to guarantee child Python model termination, (3) measure true Metal unified memory RSS from the listening worker child, and (4) hook idle reaping to Protocol 128 session timers will guarantee 100% memory reclamation (~4.7 GiB) and eliminate zombie daemon leaks.
falsification_criteria: After executing `stop_server`, any child python process remains listening on :8080, memory RSS fails to reflect the model weight allocation, or client TCP sockets are returned by port discovery.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to frontier model only if child process signal forwarding encounters macOS SIP permission errors

evidence.details: Pre-registered. RED on the old code: 4/4 defects reproduced with a stub launcher->worker tree (discovery returned a client PID; stop left the worker listening; stop reported 'stopped' while a worker ignoring SIGTERM survived; status reported the launcher). After the fix: 20/20 stub cycles and 8/8 real-model cycles (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-4bit on spare port 8099; :8080 untouched) with verified teardown, 0 survivors, 0 client PIDs; safety rule holds (process groups containing non-MLX processes fall back to a tree kill; stale state PIDs are never signalled). Real-model footprint 4,304-4,361 MB warm; system free memory recovered about 24% -> 52% after stop. Idle reaping limited to managed servers and hooked into the Protocol 128 boot (guardian_wakeup) and closure steps. Pre-registered misses: fresh-boot footprint was 562-3,317 MB (>=4,000 predicted) and ps RSS was not <100 MB for fresh servers; the warm measurement point was added after the miss and labelled as an amendment.

lessons_learned: The mission's literal lsof command (lsof -ti -sTCP:LISTEN :PORT) is invalid on macOS; use lsof -nP -iTCP:PORT -sTCP:LISTEN -t. Plain lsof -ti :PORT also returns client sockets.

ps RSS is not a usable memory measure for MLX (10 MB for a 4.7 GB worker on a long-lived server because the pages are compressed; 0.3-2 GB on fresh ones); use footprint -p PID on the listening worker, and measure after a warm-up generation because the model loads lazily (fresh 0.5-3.3 GB, warm about 4.3 GB).
A stop check that compares the listener PID with the launcher PID reports success while the worker survives; verify by checking nothing listens on the port and no tracked process is alive.
Signal a process group only when every member is an MLX process; otherwise tree-kill the worker and launcher. Never signal a state-file PID that no longer looks like an MLX process.

Reaping must be limited to servers the manager started; a hand-launched persistent daemon is never reaped. Pre-register thresholds with the measurement point (fresh vs warm) stated, or the first live run can miss for a reason that is about measurement, not the code.
